bank.name: Freedom Movement
bank.subject: Pakistan Affairs
bank.description: From the Aligarh movement and the Muslim League to partition: the political milestones of the struggle for Pakistan.

questions.prompt: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh?
questions.explanation: MAO College was founded in 1875 and later became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

questions.prompt: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's movement for Muslim educational and social reform is known as?
questions.explanation: The Aligarh Movement, led by Sir Syed, aimed at modern education for Muslims.

questions.prompt: Who was the first President of the All-India Muslim League?
questions.explanation: Aga Khan III was the first President of the Muslim League (1906-1913).

questions.prompt: The founding of the Muslim League in 1906 was mainly due to the efforts of?
questions.explanation: Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka hosted the 1906 Dhaka session where the Muslim League was founded.

questions.prompt: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was signed between?
questions.explanation: The 1916 Lucknow Pact was a compromise between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

questions.prompt: Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in which year?
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam joined the Muslim League in 1913, before which he was a Congress member.

questions.prompt: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led in India by which brothers?
questions.explanation: The Ali Brothers, Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, led the Khilafat Movement.

questions.prompt: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, introducing diarchy in the provinces, were enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced diarchy in the provinces.

questions.prompt: Which Indian leader led the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920.

questions.prompt: The all-white Simon Commission visited India in which year?
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928 and was met with the 'Simon Go Back' boycott.

questions.prompt: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by which committee?
questions.explanation: The Nehru Report, rejecting separate electorates, was produced by the Motilal Nehru Committee in 1928.

questions.prompt: The First Round Table Conference was held in which city and year?
questions.explanation: The First Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931.

questions.prompt: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by which British Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932.

questions.prompt: The Government of India Act of which year introduced provincial autonomy?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy and was the basis for the 1937 elections.

questions.prompt: In the 1937 provincial elections, which party swept the general seats?
questions.explanation: Congress won a majority in most provinces in 1937, while the Muslim League won only a small share of Muslim seats.

questions.prompt: Which day did the Muslim League observe after the resignation of Congress ministries in 1939?
questions.explanation: 22 December 1939 was observed as the Day of Deliverance after Congress ministries resigned.

questions.prompt: In the 1945-46 elections, the Muslim League's performance was?
questions.explanation: The Muslim League won all 30 reserved Muslim seats in the Central Assembly and most provincial Muslim seats.

questions.prompt: The Cabinet Mission visited India in which year?
questions.explanation: The three-member Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946.

questions.prompt: Which day is associated with the Muslim League's call for Direct Action in 1946?
questions.explanation: 16 August 1946 was observed as Direct Action Day to press for the creation of Pakistan.

questions.prompt: The Mountbatten Plan for the partition of India was announced on?
questions.explanation: The 3 June 1947 Plan, also called the Mountbatten Plan, proposed partition and the creation of Pakistan.

questions.prompt: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent in which month of 1947?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.prompt: Who became the first Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of India, while Jinnah was Pakistan's first.

questions.prompt: The Quaid-e-Azam addressed the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on?
questions.explanation: On 11 August 1947 Jinnah delivered his famous address on unity, faith and discipline.

questions.prompt: What was the national motto chosen by Quaid-e-Azam for Pakistan?
questions.explanation: 'Unity, Faith, Discipline' (Ittihad, Yaqeen, Nizam) is Pakistan's national motto.

questions.prompt: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah passed away on?
questions.explanation: The Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.

questions.prompt: The Liaquat-Nehru Pact of 1950 mainly dealt with?
questions.explanation: The 1950 pact between Liaquat Ali Khan and Nehru aimed to protect minority rights after partition.

questions.prompt: The Bogra Formula of 1953 was presented by?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the Bogra Formula as an alternative constitutional framework.

questions.prompt: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan held its first session in?
questions.explanation: The first Constituent Assembly met on 10 August 1947, with Jinnah elected as its President.

questions.prompt: The Simla Deputation of 1906 was led by whom?
questions.explanation: Aga Khan III led the Muslim deputation to Viceroy Minto in Simla in 1906.

questions.prompt: The All India Muslim League was founded in which city?
questions.explanation: The Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906.

questions.prompt: The famous 'Lucknow Pact' of 1916 was signed between?
options: The Muslim League and the Congress
questions.explanation: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was an agreement between the Muslim League and Indian National Congress.

questions.prompt: The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was launched to?
options: Protect the Ottoman caliphate after World War I
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement protested the dismemberment of the Ottoman caliphate by the Allies.

questions.prompt: Who led the Khilafat Movement in India?
options: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali
questions.explanation: The Ali brothers — Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali — led the Khilafat Movement.

questions.prompt: The Nehru Report of 1928 was rejected by Jinnah because?
options: It ignored Muslim demands for separate electorates and safeguards
questions.explanation: Jinnah's amendments to the Nehru Report were rejected, prompting his Fourteen Points.

questions.prompt: The '3 June Plan' of 1947 announced the partition of India. Who announced it?
questions.explanation: Viceroy Mountbatten announced the partition plan on 3 June 1947.

questions.prompt: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.prompt: Quaid-e-Azam took oath as Governor-General of Pakistan on?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was sworn in as the first Governor-General on 15 August 1947.

questions.prompt: The 'Cripps Mission' of 1942 offered India?
options: Dominion status after the war with a constituent assembly
questions.explanation: Cripps proposed post-war dominion status; both major parties rejected it.

questions.prompt: The 'Quit India Movement' was launched by the Congress in?
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched Quit India in August 1942.

questions.prompt: The 'Cabinet Mission' of 1946 proposed?
options: A three-tier federal plan to keep India united
questions.explanation: The 1946 Cabinet Mission proposed a loose federation, which both sides eventually rejected.

questions.prompt: The 'August Offer' of 1940 was made by which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: Linlithgow's August Offer promised post-war dominion status and constitutional talks.

questions.prompt: The 'Shimla Conference' of 1945 was called by?
questions.explanation: Wavell convened the 1945 Shimla Conference to form an interim government.

questions.prompt: The 'Muslim League' originally supported which stance in 1906?
options: Separate electorates and loyalty to the British Crown
questions.explanation: The early League sought separate electorates and British protection for Muslim interests.

questions.prompt: The 'Two-Nation Theory' was articulated most clearly in which address?
questions.explanation: Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad Address proposed a separate Muslim homeland in the northwest.

questions.prompt: The 'Delhi Muslim Proposals' of 1927 were put forward by?
options: The Muslim League led by Jinnah
questions.explanation: Jinnah's 1927 proposals sought constitutional safeguards for Muslims.

questions.prompt: The 'Nehru Report' was authored by a committee headed by?
questions.explanation: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee that produced the 1928 Nehru Report.

questions.prompt: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was between?
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact modified the Communal Award's separate electorates for depressed classes.

questions.prompt: The Government of India Act of 1935 introduced?
options: Provincial autonomy and a federal structure
questions.explanation: The 1935 Act granted provincial autonomy with elected provincial governments.

questions.prompt: In the 1937 provincial elections, the Muslim League's performance was?
options: Weak overall, winning few Muslim seats
questions.explanation: The League performed poorly in 1937, prompting organizational reforms under Jinnah.

questions.prompt: The 'Pakistan Resolution' was originally called the?
questions.explanation: It was passed as the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940.

questions.prompt: Who drafted the 'Now or Never' pamphlet that coined 'Pakistan'?
questions.explanation: Rahmat Ali, studying at Cambridge, coined 'Pakistan' in 1933.

questions.prompt: The letters of 'Pakistan' stand for?
options: Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan
questions.explanation: The name encodes Punjab, Afghania (NWFP), Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan.

questions.prompt: The 'Radcliffe Award' was announced in?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe boundary awards were published on 16-17 August 1947.

questions.prompt: The 'Independence of Pakistan' was achieved on which date?
questions.explanation: Pakistan gained independence on 14 August 1947 (celebrated annually).

questions.prompt: The Rowlatt Act was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the government emergency powers.

questions.prompt: The 'Fourteen Points' of Jinnah were presented in response to:
questions.explanation: Jinnah's 14 Points (1929) answered the Nehru Report.

questions.prompt: The Allama Mashriqi founded which organisation in 1930?
questions.explanation: Allama Mashriqi founded the Khaksar Tehrik in 1930.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League won the 1946 provincial elections in which provinces?
options: Punjab, Sindh, Bengal, NWFP (majority Muslim provinces)
questions.explanation: The League swept the Muslim-majority provinces in 1946.

questions.prompt: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on:
questions.explanation: The Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.prompt: The Lahore Resolution was seconded by:
questions.explanation: Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman seconded the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

questions.prompt: Which British Prime Minister announced the plan for partition on 3 June 1947?
questions.explanation: PM Attlee announced the 3 June Plan for partition.

questions.prompt: The Khilafat Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919.

questions.prompt: The first Round Table Conference was held in:
questions.explanation: The First Round Table Conference met in London in 1930.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League observed 'Day of Deliverance' after:
questions.explanation: The League marked 22 December 1939 after Congress ministries resigned.

questions.prompt: The Radcliffe Commission drew the boundary between:
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe's commission demarcated the 1947 boundary.

questions.prompt: The famous poem 'Tarana-e-Milli' was written by:
questions.explanation: Iqbal wrote Tarana-e-Milli celebrating Muslim identity.

questions.prompt: The Cabinet Mission Plan was presented in:
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission visited India in March–June 1946.

questions.prompt: The partition of Bengal was annulled in:
questions.explanation: The annulment of Bengal's partition came in 1911.

questions.prompt: The Pirpur Report (1938) was prepared by the Muslim League against:
questions.explanation: The Pirpur Report documented grievances under Congress ministries.

questions.prompt: The 'Punjab Unionist Party' leader who opposed partition initially was:
questions.explanation: Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan led the Unionist Party in Punjab.

questions.prompt: The first session of the All-India Muslim League was held in:
questions.explanation: The League's first session was held in Karachi in 1907.

questions.prompt: Which English daily newspaper did Jinnah edit in 1938?
questions.explanation: Jinnah launched and edited Dawn in 1938.

questions.prompt: The Lucknow Session of the Muslim League (1937) was presided over by:
questions.explanation: Jinnah presided over the League's Lucknow session in 1937.

questions.prompt: The term 'Pakistan' was coined in a pamphlet published in:
questions.explanation: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali's pamphlet 'Now or Never' (1933) coined the name.

questions.prompt: The Mountbatten Plan was also known as:
questions.explanation: Mountbatten's plan for partition is the 3 June 1947 Plan.

questions.prompt: Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly met on:
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly of Pakistan first met on 10 August 1947.

questions.prompt: The 'All-India Muslim League' was formed at which location in 1906?
questions.explanation: The League was founded at the Dacca session in December 1906.

questions.prompt: The 'Partition of Bengal' in 1905 was carried out by:
questions.explanation: Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905.

questions.prompt: The 'Minto-Morley Reforms' were introduced in:
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1909 was the Minto-Morley Reforms.

questions.prompt: The first woman president of the Indian National Congress was:
questions.explanation: Annie Besant presided over Congress in 1917.

questions.prompt: The 'Chaudhry Rahmat Ali' proposed the name 'Pakistan' in:
questions.explanation: Rahmat Ali coined 'Pakistan' in his 1933 pamphlet.

questions.prompt: The 'Wavell Plan' was announced in:
questions.explanation: The Wavell Plan was announced in June 1945.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League won how many seats in the 1945–46 central assembly elections?
questions.explanation: The League swept all Muslim seats in the centre in 1945–46.

questions.prompt: The '1946 Cabinet Mission' proposed:
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed a loose federation.

questions.prompt: Jinnah's 'Two Nation Theory' was based on:
questions.explanation: The theory stressed the distinct identity of Muslims as a nation.

questions.prompt: The 'Lahore Resolution' was originally called the:
questions.explanation: It was passed as the Pakistan Resolution on 23 March 1940.

questions.prompt: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Muslim League in 1940?
questions.explanation: Jinnah presided over the historic 1940 session.

questions.prompt: The 'Kashmir' accession to Pakistan was urged by whom in 1947?
options: The Muslim majority and tribal fighters
questions.explanation: Kashmir's Muslim majority and tribal fighters supported accession to Pakistan.

questions.prompt: The 'Radcliffe Award' was announced on:
questions.explanation: The boundary award was published on 17 August 1947.

questions.prompt: The 'Pakistani Flag' was designed by:
options: Ameer-ud-Din Khidwai (based on a design by Syed Amir-ud-din Kedwaii)
questions.explanation: The national flag design was adapted from a proposal by Ameer-ud-Din Khidwai.

questions.prompt: The 'Shimla Deputation' of 1906 demanded:
questions.explanation: The deputation sought separate Muslim electorates.

questions.prompt: The Second Round Table Conference was held in which year?
questions.explanation: The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931.

questions.prompt: The Third Round Table Conference was held in which year?
questions.explanation: The Third Round Table Conference took place in 1932.

questions.prompt: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: Gandhi and Lord Irwin signed the pact in March 1931.

questions.prompt: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact ended which movement?
questions.explanation: The pact suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.prompt: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in 1929.

questions.prompt: The Hijrat Movement of 1920 encouraged Muslims to migrate to?
questions.explanation: The Hijrat Movement urged Muslims to migrate to Afghanistan.

questions.prompt: The Swaraj Party was founded in which year by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru?
questions.explanation: The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923.

questions.prompt: The Moplah rebellion of 1921 took place in which region?
questions.explanation: The Moplah rebellion occurred in Malabar, Kerala.

questions.prompt: The Urdu-Hindi controversy that influenced Sir Syed arose after which event?
questions.explanation: The 1867 language dispute in Banaras convinced Sir Syed of the need for separate political organisation.

questions.prompt: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society in which year?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed established the Scientific Society at Ghazipur in 1863.

questions.prompt: The journal 'Tehzeeb-ul-Akhlaq' was started by whom?
questions.explanation: Sir Syed launched the journal Tehzeeb-ul-Akhlaq in 1870.

questions.prompt: The All-India Muslim League's London branch was founded in 1908 by whom?
questions.explanation: Syed Ameer Ali founded the League's London branch in 1908.

questions.prompt: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.

questions.prompt: Jinnah studied law at which institution in London?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was called to the bar from Lincoln's Inn.

questions.prompt: Jinnah was known as the 'Ambassador of' what?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity in his early career.

questions.prompt: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah joined the Congress in 1906.

questions.prompt: Jinnah was elected to the Imperial Legislative Council in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah was elected to the Imperial Legislative Council in 1910.

questions.prompt: Jinnah returned permanently to India from London in which year?
questions.explanation: Jinnah returned from London in 1934 to lead the Muslim League.

questions.prompt: The 1937 Shariat Application Act was passed by which body?
questions.explanation: The Shariat Application Act was passed in 1937 by the Indian central legislature.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League was reorganized and made a mass party after which year?
questions.explanation: After the 1937 elections the League was reorganised into a mass party.

questions.prompt: In the 1946 Bengal elections, the Muslim League ministry was headed by whom?
questions.explanation: Suhrawardy led the League ministry in Bengal after 1946.

questions.prompt: In 1946, the Punjab ministry was headed by which Unionist leader?
questions.explanation: Khizr Hayat Tiwana headed the Punjab ministry in 1946.

questions.prompt: The Congress ministry in the NWFP (1946) was headed by whom?
questions.explanation: Dr. Khan Sahib headed the Congress ministry in the NWFP.

questions.prompt: The symbol used by the Muslim League in the 1946 elections was?
questions.explanation: The League used the ballot box as its election symbol in 1946.

questions.prompt: The symbol used by the Congress in the 1946 elections was?
questions.explanation: The Congress used the charkha (spinning wheel) as its symbol.

questions.prompt: The Radcliffe Commission was headed by whom?
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the boundary commission in 1947.

questions.prompt: The words of Pakistan's national anthem were written by whom?
questions.explanation: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the national anthem's lyrics.

questions.prompt: Quaid-e-Azam is known as the?
questions.explanation: Jinnah is revered as the Father of the Nation.

questions.prompt: The Allama Iqbal's famous address at Allahabad was delivered in which year?
questions.explanation: Iqbal delivered the Allahabad Address at the 1930 League session.

questions.prompt: The Muslim League session at which Iqbal delivered his address was held in?
questions.explanation: The 1930 session was held at Allahabad.

questions.prompt: Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed is credited with first addressing Jinnah by which title?
questions.explanation: Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed is credited with conferring the title Quaid-e-Azam on Jinnah.

questions.prompt: The Pakistan National Movement was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Choudhry Rahmat Ali founded the Pakistan National Movement.

questions.prompt: The partition of Bengal in 1905 divided Bengal for administrative purposes into?
questions.explanation: The 1905 partition divided Bengal into eastern and western parts.

questions.prompt: The Muslims of Bengal celebrated the annulment of the partition in 1911 as?
questions.explanation: Muslims had supported the 1905 partition and were aggrieved by its annulment in 1911.

questions.prompt: The Swadeshi Movement (1905) was launched in protest against?
questions.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement protested the partition of Bengal.

questions.prompt: The Lahore Resolution was moved by whom at the 1940 session?
questions.explanation: A.K. Fazlul Haq moved the Lahore Resolution.

questions.prompt: The Quaid-e-Azam's final illness and death occurred in which city?
questions.explanation: Jinnah died in Karachi on 11 September 1948.

questions.prompt: The 'Independence Day' of Pakistan is celebrated on which date?
questions.explanation: Pakistan celebrates Independence Day on 14 August.

questions.prompt: The 'Pakistan Day' is celebrated on which date?
questions.explanation: Pakistan Day commemorates the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940.
